items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: I mean, you know, like Bessie Smith and Manly Smith and all of them.

ctx.x: Now what about in playing trumpet behind the singers? How did that develop?

Well, we used to do it. When the singer, singer, say and listen and cut out, we fill in. But now they go right along with the singer, you know what I mean? Like somebody say, I've got the blues and the blues about to kill me. I've got the blues and the blues about to kill me. And if I lose the blues, I won't be. You know what I mean? That's what we used to play. When the singer cut out, we come in. When she come back, we cut out. Drop under, you know. But now they go right along with the singer. Who would sing…
Did anybody use a plunger down here? Well, there was until after that.
